items.title: Section: Approaching a Spiritual Friend Correctly — Serving Through Illness and Health, and Genuine Obedience Without Wavering

items.zh: 當知菩薩由四種相，方得圓滿親近善友。一、於善友有病無病隨時供侍，恒常發起愛敬淨信。二、於善友隨時敬問、禮拜、奉迎、合掌、慇懃，修和敬業而為供養。三、於善友如法衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥資身什物隨時供養。四、於善友若正依止，於如法義若合若離，隨自在轉，無有傾動，如實顯發，作奉教心，隨時往詣恭敬、承事、請問、聽受。
items.en: One should understand that bodhisattvas, through four marks, come to approach a spiritual friend in a genuinely complete way. First, attending on a spiritual friend at all times, whether they are sick or well, constantly raising love, respect, and pure faith. Second, respectfully greeting, prostrating before, welcoming, and joining palms towards a spiritual friend at all times, earnestly cultivating harmonious, respectful conduct as an offering. Third, supplying a spiritual friend at all times with properly, lawfully obtained robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicine for illness, and every article supporting the body. Fourth, taking a spiritual friend as one's genuine basis of reliance, freely and correctly acting in accordance with the true dharma's own meaning, whether accepting what accords with it or releasing what does not, without any wavering; genuinely disclosing any fault as it actually is; holding a mind of pure obedience to the teaching; and going again and again to respectfully attend upon, ask questions of, and receive what is taught.

items.title: Section: Listening to the Dharma Opens — Regarding It as a Rare Jewel, and as the Eye That Will See Everything Knowable

items.zh: 若諸菩薩欲聽法時，作五種想，應從善友聽聞正法。一、作寶想。難得義故。二、作眼想。能得廣大俱生妙慧因性義故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who wish to listen to the dharma should form five kinds of thought when listening to the true teaching from a spiritual friend. First, regarding it as a jewel, because of how genuinely difficult it is to obtain. Second, regarding it as an eye, because it forms the cause for obtaining the vast, spontaneously arising, wondrous wisdom of complete awakening.

items.title: Section: Listening to the Dharma Closes — As Light Illuminating Every Phenomenon Equally, As the Cause of Nirvāṇa, and as Faultless Joy Drawn From the Seven Noble Treasures

items.zh: 三、作明想。已得廣大俱生慧眼，於一切種如實所知等照義故。四、作大果勝功德想。能得涅槃及三菩提無上妙迹因性義故。五、作無罪大適悅想。於現法中未得涅槃及三菩提，於法如實簡擇止觀無罪大樂因性義故。
items.en: Third, regarding it as light, because it forms the cause for the vast, spontaneously arising eye of wisdom already obtained, illuminating every kind of knowable phenomenon exactly as it is, equally and without distinction. Fourth, regarding it as a great and excellent fruit, because it forms the cause for nirvāṇa and complete awakening's own unsurpassed, wondrous path. Fifth, regarding it as a faultless, deeply satisfying joy, because, even in this present life, before nirvāṇa and complete awakening have yet been attained, it forms the cause for the faultless, great happiness of correctly discerning the dharma through calming and insight practice.

items.title: Section: Never Judging the Teacher — Broken Precepts, Low Birth, and an Unlovely Face Are Never Grounds to Refuse the Teaching

items.zh: 若諸菩薩欲從善友聽聞法時，於說法師由五種處不作異意，以純淨心屬耳聽法。一、於壞戒不作異意。謂不作心：此是破戒，不住律儀，我今不應從彼聽法。二、於壞族不作異意。謂不作心：此是卑姓，我今不應從彼聽法。三、於壞色不作異意。謂不作心：此是醜陋，我今不應從彼聽法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who wish to listen to the dharma from a spiritual friend should never form a contrary opinion of the teacher on five points, but should instead listen to the teaching with a wholly pure mind, ears genuinely attentive. First, never forming a contrary opinion regarding broken discipline: that is, never thinking, "this teacher has broken the precepts and does not abide in proper discipline; I ought not listen to the teaching from them now." Second, never forming a contrary opinion regarding humble lineage: that is, never thinking, "this teacher is of a lowly family; I ought not listen to the teaching from them now." Third, never forming a contrary opinion regarding an unlovely appearance: that is, never thinking, "this teacher is unsightly; I ought not listen to the teaching from them now."

items.title: Section: Rely on Meaning, Not on Rhetoric — Approaching Good Friends Closes With a Warning Against Squandering Wisdom Through Pettiness

items.zh: 四、於壞文不作異意。謂不作心：此於言詞不善藻飾，我今不應從彼聽法。但依於義，不應依文。五、於壞美不作異意。謂不作心：此語麁惡，多懷忿恚，不以美言宣說諸法，我今不應從彼聽法。如是菩薩欲聽法時，於是五處不應作意，但應恭敬攝受正法，於說法師未嘗見過。若有菩薩其慧微劣，於說法師心生嫌鄙，不欲從其聽聞正法，當知此行不求自利，退失勝慧。
items.en: Fourth, never forming a contrary opinion regarding unrefined phrasing: that is, never thinking, "this teacher's words are not skilfully embellished; I ought not listen to the teaching from them now." One should rely upon the meaning, not upon the phrasing. Fifth, never forming a contrary opinion regarding blunt speech: that is, never thinking, "this teacher's words are coarse, harbouring much indignation, and this teacher does not proclaim the teaching in agreeable language; I ought not listen to the teaching from them now." Bodhisattvas who wish to listen to the dharma should never dwell on any of these five points, but should instead respectfully take up the true teaching, never once looking for fault in the teacher delivering it. Should any bodhisattva of weak, inferior wisdom form a contemptuous, disdainful opinion of a teacher and refuse to listen to the true teaching from them, one should understand that such conduct does not genuinely seek one's own benefit at all, but instead causes one's own excellent wisdom to be lost.

items.title: Section: Cultivating the Four Immeasurables Opens — Three Depths From Sentient Beings to Mere Phenomena to No Object at All

items.zh: 云何菩薩修四無量慈、悲、喜、捨？謂諸菩薩略有三種修四無量。一者、有情緣無量，二者、法緣無量，三者、無緣無量。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas cultivate the four immeasurables of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity? Bodhisattvas cultivate the four immeasurables, in brief, in three ways: first, the immeasurables taking sentient beings as their object; second, the immeasurables taking mere phenomena as their object; third, the immeasurables taking no object at all.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於其三聚一切有情，安立以為無苦無樂、有苦、有樂。

items.title: Section: Loving-Kindness Defined Across Three Depths, Then the Same Structure Extended to the Remaining Three

items.zh: 於其最初欲求樂者，發起與樂增上意樂，普緣十方，安住無倒有情勝解，修慈俱心，當知是名有情緣慈。若諸菩薩，住唯法想增上意樂，正觀唯法假說有情，修慈俱心，當知即此名法緣慈。若諸菩薩，復於諸法遠離分別，修慈俱心，當知即此名無緣慈。如有情緣、法緣、無緣三慈差別，悲、喜、捨三，當知亦爾。若諸菩薩，於有苦者，發起除苦增上意樂，普緣十方修悲俱心，是名為悲。若諸菩薩，於有樂者，發起隨喜增上意樂，普緣十方修喜俱心，是名為喜。若諸菩薩，即於如是無苦無樂、有苦、有樂三種有情，隨其次第，發起遠離癡瞋貪惑增上意樂，普緣十方修捨俱心，是名為捨。
items.en: Towards the first of these three groups — those who wish for happiness —, raising the heightened aspiration to give happiness, universally extended across the ten directions, resting in an undistorted, correct understanding of beings, and cultivating a mind joined with loving-kindness — one should understand this to be called loving-kindness taking sentient beings as its object. Bodhisattvas who abide in the heightened aspiration of regarding beings as mere phenomena, correctly observing that "sentient beings" is only a provisional label for mere phenomena, and who cultivate a mind joined with loving-kindness on this basis — one should understand this to be called loving-kindness taking mere phenomena as its object. Bodhisattvas who, further still, remain entirely free of conceptual discrimination towards all phenomena while cultivating a mind joined with loving-kindness — one should understand this to be called loving-kindness taking no object at all. Just as loving-kindness differs across these three — sentient beings, mere phenomena, and no object — one should understand that compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity are exactly the same. Bodhisattvas who, towards those in suffering, raise the heightened aspiration to remove suffering, universally extended across the ten directions, cultivating a mind joined with compassion — this is called compassion. Bodhisattvas who, towards those who have happiness, raise the heightened aspiration to rejoice with them, universally extended across the ten directions, cultivating a mind joined with sympathetic joy — this is called sympathetic joy. Bodhisattvas who, towards these same three kinds of being — those with neither suffering nor happiness, those with suffering, and those with happiness — raise, in proper sequence, the heightened aspiration to release delusion, hostility, and craving, universally extended across the ten directions, cultivating a mind joined with equanimity — this is called equanimity.

items.title: Section: Uncommon Even Among Śrāvakas — What the Bodhisattva's Four Immeasurables Share With Outsiders, With the Two Vehicles, and With No One Else at All

items.zh: 此中菩薩慈等無量有情緣者，當知其相與外道共。若法緣者，當知其相與諸聲聞及獨覺共，不共外道。若無緣者，當知其相不共一切聲聞、獨覺，及諸外道。又諸菩薩三種無量，應知安樂意樂所攝，謂慈、悲、喜。一種無量，應知利益意樂所攝，是謂為捨。如是菩薩一切無量，名為哀愍。以諸菩薩成就此故，名哀愍者。
items.en: Among these, one should understand that the bodhisattva's loving-kindness and the rest, when taking sentient beings as their object, share their character with outsiders. When taking mere phenomena as their object, one should understand that their character is shared with śrāvakas and solitary realisers, but not with outsiders. When taking no object at all, one should understand that their character is shared with none of these — not śrāvakas, not solitary realisers, and not outsiders. Furthermore, one should understand that three of the bodhisattva's immeasurables — loving-kindness, compassion, and sympathetic joy — are gathered under the aspiration for happiness, while the remaining one, equanimity, is gathered under the aspiration for genuine benefit. Bodhisattvas cultivating every one of the immeasurables in this way are called ones of genuine compassion; it is precisely because bodhisattvas accomplish this that they are named ones of genuine compassion.

blocks.text: How to approach a teacher, how to listen, and the bodhisattva's four immeasurables.

Attending on them "whether sick or well"; respectful; obedient "without wavering, with a mind of following the teaching". Master Cháng Bǎi: the friend relied on is the one through whom one turns from ordinary to noble.

Regard the Dharma as a **jewel** ("so hard to find"; Master Cháng Bǎi: many stones, very few diamonds); as an **eye** that will see everything knowable; as **light**; as a **great fruit** ("the cause of nirvāṇa and awakening"); and as faultless joy.

Do not refuse the teaching because of the teacher's broken precepts, low birth, unattractive appearance, unrefined phrasing, or harsh speech. Master Cháng Bǎi: a teacher's looks have nothing to do with the Dharma; even one of low birth who has attained arhatship should be heard. "Rely on meaning, not on words."

Taking **beings** as object; taking **mere phenomena** as object; and with **no object** at all. Master Cháng Bǎi: not clinging to the idea that one is practising, the three spheres empty: that is without object.
With beings as object, the immeasurables are shared with outsiders; with phenomena as object, with śrāvakas; without object, they are the bodhisattva's alone.

quiz.q: What is the fourth mark of approaching a spiritual friend completely?
options: relying correctly, unwavering, with an obedient mind, visiting to serve, ask, and listen
quiz.why: "Fourth, correctly relying on a spiritual friend … without wavering, with a mind of obeying the teaching, visiting at proper times to serve, ask, and listen." Master Cháng Bǎi: no wish to trouble the teacher, only to understand the dharma — that is "a mind obedient to instruction."

quiz.q: The first thought in listening, "regarding it as a jewel because it is rare" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: stones are many, diamonds few; reciting the sūtra-opening verse before class reminds us to treasure the dharma
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: there are many stones but very few diamonds; reciting the sūtra-opening verse before each class reminds us to treasure the dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: worldly treasures are hard to obtain — only those of great merit get them.

quiz.q: Why regard the dharma as "a great and excellent fruit"?
options: it is the cause for attaining nirvāṇa and supreme awakening
quiz.why: "Fourth, regarding it as a great and excellent fruit, because it is the cause for attaining nirvāṇa and supreme awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: nirvāṇa is the quality of elimination, awakening the quality of wisdom.

quiz.q: Of the five points on which one should not judge the teacher, what are the first three?
options: broken discipline, low birth, unattractive appearance
quiz.why: Not judging regarding broken discipline, low birth, or unattractive appearance. Master Cháng Bǎi: a teacher's looks have nothing to do with the teaching.

quiz.q: "Not judging unrefined phrasing … rely on meaning, not wording" — what do the lectures say?
options: though the words are rustic, the meaning is precious — rely on meaning, not elegant words
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in hearing the dharma, rely on meaning, not words — attend to what the words express, not to their beauty. Venerable Miào Jìng: the phrasing may be rustic, but the meaning inside is precious.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, in what three ways do bodhisattvas cultivate the four immeasurables?
options: taking beings, mere phenomena, and no object as object
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas cultivate the four immeasurables, in brief, in three ways: first, taking sentient beings as object; second, taking mere phenomena as object; third, taking no object." Master Cháng Bǎi: three kinds, from shallow to deep.

quiz.q: With whom is each of the three kinds shared, and how do the lectures explain why?
options: beings-object shared with outsiders, phenomena-object with the two vehicles, no-object with none; Miào Jìng: outsiders don't know non-self, the two vehicles don't know phenomena are empty; Cháng Bǎi: outsiders seek Brahmā rebirth, the two vehicles still grasp phenomena
quiz.why: The beings-object kind is shared with outsiders; the phenomena-object kind with śrāvakas and solitary realisers; the no-object kind with no one. Venerable Miào Jìng: outsiders do not know non-self; śrāvakas and solitary realisers do not know that all verbally established phenomena are ultimately empty. Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders cultivate them to be reborn in the Brahmā heavens; the two vehicles still grasp phenomena.
